headline: Rafaela grand slam lifts Red Sox in thriller out in California
morning_brew: What a wild, tension-filled night out at Sutter Health Park. We spent most of the game staring at zeroes on the scoreboard, and I was about two seconds away from throwing my Dunks at the TV, wondering if the bats had collectively decided to take the day off. Then Ceddanne Rafaela stepped up and absolutely crushed that grand slam in the sixth. It was exactly the kind of bolt of lightning this lineup needed to wake the hell up. Payton Tolle gave us some real quality innings, and our bullpen, which usually scares the life out of me, actually shut the door with surgical precision to ensure we walked away with the result.

The news about Curtis Mead is a real gut punch, though. Seeing him exit his debut after that pitch caught him on the wrist is a total disaster for a guy we just brought in to help move the needle. You hope it is just a minor thing and he is back in the mix sooner rather than later, because losing an acquisition that fast is just our miserable luck sometimes. I am keeping my fingers crossed that the trainers have some good news when they check him again today, but I have seen this movie before and it usually ends with a trip to the IL.

Winning eighteen of our last twenty has really changed the vibe around the club, and it finally feels like we are playing the way we know we can. I am not saying I am putting a deposit in the Duck Boat fund just yet, but this team is cooking. We have to keep grinding through this road trip, but taking the opener against the Athletics is a solid way to start the week. Let's see if the guys can keep the energy high tonight. I am not going to get ahead of myself, but it is nice to watch a team that actually looks focused on the prize.

news_digest.headline: Curtis Mead exits Red Sox debut with left wrist contusion
news_digest.dans_take: Tough luck for the newcomer, hopefully it is nothing that keeps him out for long, because my heart cannot take any more of this.

news_digest.headline: Ceddanne Rafaela's grand slam sends Red Sox past A's 4-2
news_digest.dans_take: That grand slam was the spark we needed to turn a quiet, miserable night into a sweet victory.

trend_watch.trend: Hit his first major league grand slam
trend_watch.dans_take: That swing was pure gold and changed the entire complexion of the night from a snoozefest to a party.

trend_watch.trend: Three strikeouts in a scoreless ninth
trend_watch.dans_take: The man was throwing absolute gas out there, and for once I did not have to watch the ninth inning through my fingers.

trend_watch.trend: Held hitless in two at bats
trend_watch.dans_take: He has been a force lately, but every guy gets a night where the timing is just a little off, like my neighbor Rick after his third espresso.
